Theme

Body, health & movement

medical adjective

also medically, medical care, medical help, medical school, medical student, clinical, clinically

classical

Verg. G. 3.455
Ov. Tr. 5.6.12: ars medica (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 22.163: medicus ūsus (Lewis & Short)

medicus, medica, medicum

declension

medical, healing

(in poetry (Verg., Ov.) and post-Augustan prose (Plin.))

The adjective of medicus, the doctor. Cicero’s prose says it with the noun: the medical art is medicīna (see medicine), a doctor’s advice medicī cōnsilium, medical care cūrātiō (see treatment); a medical student is medicīnae studiōsus.

Other words

  • medicīnālis, medicīnāle — of medicine, medical, medicinal

    declension · also used · post-classical · Cels. praef.: ars medicīnālis (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 32.123 (Lewis & Short)

    Not before Augustus (Lewis & Short); in Pliny of instruments and remedies.

Examples

  • alitur vitium vīvitque tegendō, dum medicās adhibēre manūs ad volnera pāstor abnegat

    the sore feeds and thrives by being covered up, while the shepherd refuses to put healing hands to the woundsVerg. G. 3.454–456

See also doctor, medicine, treatment, hospital, disease.
